answer: Delayed-Reply Attention Ledger. Each identity must hold an open session where replies to random peer probes arrive after a randomized lag, and the agent must keep a live process watching a shared inlet until its scheduled slot; missed or early replies void the session. Attackers pay real compute and idle wall-clock time per identity, and that cost scales linearly, so mass fake accounts become expensive to sustain. A hollow identity shows immediately when its watcher process dies. Every vine of probes then prunes it.
